prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Kāneikokala, the kindly Hawaiian shark ancestor returning a canoe-wreck survivor safely to shore.
ANATOMY: ONE powerful natural GREY SHARK, one head, TWO dark natural eyes, normal shark mouth CLOSED, one dorsal fin, TWO pectoral fins, paired pelvic fins and one vertical tail; no horns, tattoos, human face, glowing eyes or invented anatomy [kaneikokala-c05,kaneikokala-c11].
MOMENT: Swim strongly toward a visible Hawaiian island shore, huge foreground shark viewed from a split waterline low angle, head angled toward viewer but travel direction diagonal shoreward. ONE fully clothed ADULT survivor beside dorsal fin holds a small plain wooden canoe float, safe, alert and relieved, gently carried in the shark's wake. No touching mouth, no teeth, biting, fear, injury or violence. A broken canoe plank behind explains rescue without wrecked bodies.
POWER: a kindly protector saves canoe-wreck survivors and returns them to home islands; active calm guidance through moving water, no magical energy [kaneikokala-c03,kaneikokala-c06,kaneikokala-c11].
SCALE & CAMERA: low split waterline close view makes shark's face and forward body dominate square, adult and island are secondary, natural shark scale through perspective, not giant monster.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one golden sunset lights shark under surface and wet adult above, deep walnut sea shadows, ordinary rolling swell and translucent spray.
SURFACE: natural matte grey shark skin, water droplets, worn floating wood, fully opaque wet simple clothing.
SETTING: ocean approaching Hawaiian home island, green shore clearly ahead [kaneikokala-c06].
MOOD: reverent awe and gratitude for a powerful kindly ancestral guardian, active rescue, never threatening predator, cute pet or ordinary shark portrait.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, inscriptions, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra heads, limbs or fingers; no design borrowed from any film, game, anime or comic; no nudity or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outline or energy ribbons. Premium painterly brushwork, dark warm walnut and antique gold palette, square composition.
name: Kāneikokala
rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

visual_review.notes: Native and 200px inspected: one natural shark with closed mouth, correct paired pectoral fins/dorsal/tail, no fantasy markings. Shark dominates split-water view while safe adult holding canoe float follows beside dorsal fin, looking toward nearby island shore; broken wood secondary. Strong forward rescue movement and protector relation readable at 200px, no attack. No glow, teeth display, text, gore or invented anatomy. Seven Sangar checks pass.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and survivor and fin crops. One natural grey shark dominates a split-waterline frame: one head, two eyes, mouth closed with no teeth shown, one dorsal fin, two pectoral fins, pelvic and anal fins and one heterocercal tail. There are no tattoos, glow or invented anatomy (shark aumakua, kaneikokala-c05/c11). Above the water, one fully clothed adult survivor of a broken canoe (shirt, both hands on a plank, five fingers) rides beside the dorsal fin, looking relieved toward the green Hawaiian shore and mountains ahead. Broken canoe wood trails behind. This shows the documented act of saving canoe-wreck survivors and bringing them home to shore (c03/c06/c11), so it reads as the protector's rescue, not an ordinary shark or an attack. Golden sunset, powerful foreground scale, no gore or text.
